gene.meaning: A small part of our body's instruction book. We each have two copies of most genes, one from each parent.

carrier.meaning: Someone who has a change in one copy of a gene but usually has no sign of the condition. Being a carrier is not the same as having the condition.

recessive.meaning: A condition appears only when a child receives a changed copy from both parents. Each carrier parent passes it on about half the time.

xlinked.meaning: A gene on the X chromosome. Sons and daughters can be affected differently because they carry different sex chromosomes.

related.meaning: Relatives are more likely to share the same gene changes because they have common ancestors. This can raise the chance for some conditions.

estimate.meaning: A chance worked out from known facts. It is not a diagnosis and not a promise about any one child.

uncertain.meaning: Sometimes a test cannot give a clear answer. No chance is given until a counsellor helps work out the next step.

confirmatory.meaning: A further test that can clarify a result. A counsellor can explain what it involves.

counsellor.meaning: A trained professional who explains results, answers questions and supports your choices without telling you what to do.

consent.meaning: Your choice about who may see what. You can stop sharing at any time.

myths.fact: Most carriers have no sign of the condition. Being a carrier is not the same as having it.

myths.myth: A chance means it will happen.
myths.fact: A chance is not a certainty. A one-in-four chance means most pregnancies are not affected.

myths.myth: Someone is to blame for a gene change.
myths.fact: Gene changes are common and nobody chooses them. Nobody caused this.

myths.myth: The result tells us what to decide.
myths.fact: The result gives information. What to do next is always your choice, with support if you want it.
Nothing is shared unless you choose. You can stop sharing in one tap.
No test finds everything, and being related can leave a very small chance. A counsellor can explain.

talk.t1: I had a health screening and I would like to tell you about it. Nothing is wrong with you or with me.
talk.t2: The screening looks at family health, not at blame. There is a counsellor who can explain it better than I can.
talk.t3: You may want to talk to a counsellor yourself. It is private and it is your choice.
talk.t4: I would like us to decide together what to do next, at our own pace.

kin.greet: Hello, I am Kin. I can explain your own result in plain words, explain terms, show who you share with, or take you to a page. I never tell anyone what to decide.
kin.thanks: You are welcome. Ask me anything about your own result any time.
kin.help: I can explain your own result, explain a term such as carrier or estimate, show who you share with, or open a page. What would you like?
kin.noResult: I do not have an explanation to read yet. Open My result first, then ask me again.
kin.noShare: You are not sharing anything right now.
kin.counsellor: A genetic counsellor can go through your result with you and answer questions. You can ask for one at any time, and what you do next is your choice.
kin.family: You can invite a relative so that they see only what you choose, and the family page has gentle ways to start the conversation. Nothing is shared without your agreement.
kin.how: KinSight explains a screening result in plain words, shows what it means for a couple, and keeps a counsellor in the loop. A computer program works out every number, and approved sentences explain it.
kin.settings: Use the gear icon at the top for dark mode, bigger text, high contrast and less motion. The language menu at the top switches language.
kin.sick: Being a carrier is not the same as having the condition. Most carriers have no sign of it.
chips: How do I find a counsellor?
kin.refusal: I can only help with your own result. I cannot share other people's information, give medical advice, or tell you what to decide. A genetic counsellor can talk this through with you.
